brief: The Fed raised rates to 3.75%-4% and signaled one more hike by year-end, driven by persistent inflation and commodity-price spillovers (diesel cited) outweighing growth concerns, since growth is resilient. The decision was unanimous; 12 of 16 participants' projections favored two hikes this year, and eight favor another in 2027. Warsh framed the hike as the endpoint of a months-long data-dependent process (June: reaffirmed core-PCE focus; July: waited for more evidence; September: acted), not a reaction to markets, arguing financial conditions were only barely restrictive. Growth projections were revised up, unemployment is seen staying at a low 4.1%, and the longer-run rate was nudged up to 3.2% on a more optimistic productivity view. Headline PCE is estimated at 3.6% in August (core 3.2%). Generali expects one further hike this year then a pause through 2027, arguing the four hikes markets have priced through next year are excessive because sticky inflation will erode real incomes and cap consumption. Markets read the unanimity as hawkish: two-year yields rose to 4.7%, ten-year yields topped 5%, the dollar hit a post-July high, and the S&P 500 fell 0.8%.
